articles.detail: 5 cycles all completed, avg 10/cycle (selector 316s, writer 688s, editor 383s)

experiment: Skipped. No active experiments pending evaluation, and the noNewExperimentsUntil gate (2026-05-31) still blocks new variables while the 2026-05-28 opus-4-8 selector/tune + low-effort-editor lineup baselines. All metrics are within targets. Gate drops after 2026-05-31 — do not auto-extend.
weakestArea: Regional spread is the thinnest margin: 5 regions vs the >=4 target, but Oceania was entirely absent and Africa was light at 4. EU dominated at 15/42 (36% of output) with the Americas at 10, so the geographic distribution leans heavily Euro-Atlantic even though the headline region count clears its floor.
watching: Editor held at 383s avg with all 5 cycles completing and zero timeouts under the new low-effort/opus-4-8 lineup — confirm this stays stable through tomorrow so the post-2026-05-28 baseline is clean before any new experiment.
Tech is the lowest category at 6 (floor 3/cycle, met) and leaned on CoinDesk for 5 of the day's crypto/markets coverage — watch that tech breadth doesn't narrow to crypto.
Multi-source count is healthy at 11, but history shows this rides on feed supply (~9/cycle) not selector floors; track whether it holds without intervention.
coverageGaps: Oceania had zero coverage today and only one article yesterday — recurring blind spot.
Africa thin at 4/42 despite curated African outlets (Premium Times x3, Daily Maverick) in the feed.
Tech specialist coverage concentrated in crypto/markets (CoinDesk x5) rather than spread across research/security/AI outlets.
context: Healthy, unremarkable day: 42 articles across 5 fully completed cycles (up from 31 yesterday), all five quality goals met, zero duplicates, top source under 12%. The operative constraint today is procedural, not metric-driven — the self-imposed experiment pause (set after the 2026-05-28 flip to opus-4-8 for selector/tune plus permanent low-effort editor) runs through 2026-05-31, so no tunable variable is introduced until tomorrow. Standing sourcing lesson holds: multi-source rate is capped upstream by feed clustering supply (~22% ceiling), so the next sourcing experiment should target Event Registry / regional-outlet inclusion rather than selector floors.
